claims.title: Equal 50/50 Parenting Time Best Serves the Three Minor Dependents
claims.statement: Under Uniform Domestic Relations Act § 402(a), an equal 50/50 week-on/week-off schedule (182.5 overnights each) with Wednesday school exchanges preserves caregiving continuity and emotional stability.
claims.summary: Equal 182.5-overnight schedule with mid-week school exchanges preserves historical continuity and academic performance.

claims.title: Six-Year Hands-On Caregiving & 2028 Four-Month Solo Parenting
claims.statement: From 2023 through 2029, Respondent handled daily school transport, homework, and pediatric care—including four months of solo caregiving in 2028 while Petitioner was on a regional logistics rotation.
claims.summary: Six years of primary daily caregiving and four months of solo parenting in 2028 establish deep caregiving continuity.

claims.title: Zero Tardies & Academic Excellence During 2030 90-Day 50/50 Period
claims.statement: Certified school attendance records (Ex. K) prove that during the 90-day equal 50/50 schedule in early 2030, all three dependents had zero tardies and strong academic evaluations.
claims.summary: Certified school records confirm zero tardies and high academic performance during the 90-day 50/50 schedule.

claims.title: School-Zone Residential Proximity Enables Seamless Exchanges
claims.statement: Both parents reside within the same suburban school district attendance zone (10 minutes apart), enabling conflict-free curb exchanges at school.
claims.summary: Stipulated 10-minute proximity within the school district supports week-on/week-off school exchanges.

claims.title: Joint Major Decision-Making with Mediation-First Protocol
claims.statement: Six years of cooperative educational and medical choices plus neutral portal communication support joint major decision-making with mediation prior to court intervention (Ex. L).
claims.summary: Historical cooperation on education and health care supports joint major decision-making with mediation first.

claims.title: Early Completion of Certified Co-Parenting & Communication Seminar
claims.statement: Respondent completed the 16-hour certified Co-Parenting & Communication Seminar on June 1, 2030—30 days ahead of the judicial deadline (Ex. D).
claims.summary: Completed 16-hour certified co-parenting seminar 30 days ahead of schedule.

claims.title: Stipulated Monthly Income Baseline ($8,000 Petitioner / $5,000 Respondent)
claims.statement: In the Joint Pretrial Stipulation (¶ 14), the parties stipulated to monthly gross incomes of $8,000.00/mo ($800,000 cents) for Petitioner and $5,000.00/mo ($500,000 cents) for Respondent.
claims.summary: Pretrial Stipulation fixes monthly income baseline at $8,000.00/mo Petitioner and $5,000.00/mo Respondent ($13,000.00/mo combined).

claims.title: Guideline Support Transfer Is $250.00/mo from Petitioner to Respondent
claims.statement: Applying the $13,000.00/mo combined baseline, 182.5 equal overnights, and $0 medical/childcare add-ons on Worksheet Ex. N yields a net guideline transfer of $250.00/mo ($25,000 cents) from Petitioner to Respondent.
claims.summary: Guideline Worksheet Ex. N establishes a $250.00/mo net transfer from Petitioner to Respondent.

claims.title: Statutory Disability Pension Exemption Bars Speculative Wage Imputation
claims.statement: Under Uniform Support Guidelines § 305(5)(b), Respondent's certified permanent disability pension determination (Ex. E) bars imputing speculative commercial engineering wages.
claims.summary: Certified permanent disability retirement determination (Ex. E) bars speculative income imputation under § 305(5)(b).

claims.title: Open-Source Civic Software Research Generated $0 Compensation (2026–2029 Taxes)
claims.statement: Certified IRS Tax Return Transcripts for 2026, 2027, 2028, and 2029 (Ex. I) prove Respondent received $0 in gross revenue, salary, or distributions from open-source civic software projects.
claims.summary: Four years of certified IRS transcripts (2026–2029, Ex. I) confirm $0 income from open-source civic software contributions.

claims.title: Comprehensive Statutory Dependent Medical Benefit Eliminates $180/mo Duplicate Add-On
claims.statement: All three dependents are enrolled in Respondent's statutory public-service dependent medical plan at $0 monthly premium (Ex. E), eliminating Petitioner's $180.00/mo duplicate insurance add-on on OP Ex. 2.
claims.summary: Statutory $0-premium dependent medical coverage (Ex. E) eliminates the $180/mo duplicate insurance add-on.

claims.title: Full-Time Parental Availability Eliminates $1,500/mo Third-Party After-School Vendor Add-On
claims.statement: Respondent is available full-time before and after school and during Petitioner's regional travel shifts (Ex. L), eliminating the unnecessary $1,500/mo ($450/mo worksheet share) commercial after-school agency expense.
claims.summary: Direct parental care availability (Ex. L) eliminates the $1,500/mo ($450/mo worksheet share) commercial vendor add-on.

claims.title: Petitioner Omitted $30,000.00 in Escrow Accounts x4102 & x4109 on Initial Disclosure
claims.statement: Comparison of Petitioner's June 10, 2029 Sworn Financial Statement (Ex. G) with subpoenaed bank statements (Ex. H) proves Petitioner omitted $30,000.00 ($3,000,000 cents) held in Escrow Checking x4102 and Reserve Savings x4109.
claims.summary: Subpoenaed bank statements (Ex. H) prove $30,000.00 in liquid escrow funds was omitted from the June 10, 2029 Sworn Financial Statement (Ex. G).

claims.title: Rule 16.2(e)(10) Bars Petitioner's Retroactive Support & Expense Reimbursement Demand
claims.statement: Because Petitioner omitted $30,000.00 in liquid reserves while claiming financial hardship during interim proceedings, Civil Rule 16.2(e)(10) bars retroactive expense shifting (Ex. G, Ex. H, Ex. J, Ex. N ¶¶ 24–26).
claims.summary: Material omission of $30,000.00 on the Sworn Financial Statement bars retroactive support and expense claims under Rule 16.2(e)(10).

claims.title: FRE 106 Rule of Completeness Rebuts Selective Excerpt from 2028 Homework Study Log
claims.statement: Under FRE 106, page 4 lines 10–24 of the 2028 Co-Parenting & Homework Study Log (OP Ex. 13, dated October 12, 2028) proves both parents jointly agreed on calm, non-punitive homework tutoring and positive reinforcement.
claims.summary: Full context of the 2028 Homework Study Log (OP Ex. 13, p. 4) under FRE 106 confirms calm, positive parenting.

claims.title: FRE 106 Complete Portal Thread Proves Respectful Co-Parenting & Dependent Preference
claims.statement: Admitting the complete 6-page co-parenting portal thread (OP Ex. 14, Ex. B) under FRE 106 shows Respondent calmly coordinating schedules and the 15-year-old asking to resume the 50/50 rotation.
claims.summary: Complete portal message thread (Ex. B, OP Ex. 14) under FRE 106 disproves hostile-communication allegations.

claims.title: Collateral Relative Witnesses Lack Post-2028 Personal Knowledge Under FRE 602
claims.statement: Opposing lay witnesses W-07, W-08, and W-09 admit they have not visited Respondent's residence or observed his parenting since 2028, limiting their testimony under FRE 602 and FRE 802.
claims.summary: Opposing collateral witnesses lack post-2028 personal observation under FRE 602.

claims.title: Verified 500-Yard School-Zone Transit Log Proves Full Buffer Compliance
claims.statement: Certified school check-in badge logs and transit telemetry (Ex. F, Ex. M) prove Respondent remained 512 yards from Petitioner's residence on the public arterial avenue during routine school drop-off.
claims.summary: Certified transit telemetry (512 yards, Ex. F) proves strict compliance with the 250-yard interim buffer.

claims.title: October 1, 2029 Stipulated Dismissal With Prejudice of Interim Restriction Motion
claims.statement: On October 1, 2029, Petitioner stipulated to dismiss her interim restriction motion with prejudice (Ex. C) in exchange for neutral civil standby/school-curb exchange protocols.
claims.summary: Prior restriction motion was dismissed with prejudice by stipulation on October 1, 2029 (Ex. C).

claims.title: First Right of Refusal During Multi-Day Regional Logistics Travel Shifts
claims.statement: When Petitioner travels on multi-day regional logistics shifts, the Proposed Parenting Plan (Ex. L § 4.3) grants Respondent the first right of refusal so the dependents stay with a parent rather than a commercial vendor.
claims.summary: Right of first refusal during multi-day travel shifts keeps dependents with a parent at zero cost (Ex. L).

claims.title: Suburban Single-Family Residence With Dedicated Bedrooms & Study Space
claims.statement: Photographic and property records (Ex. O) establish that Respondent's suburban residence inside the school district provides dedicated bedrooms, study desks, and a fenced yard 8 minutes from school.
claims.summary: Property and photo records (Ex. O) confirm a stable, well-equipped home 8 minutes from school.

claims.title: Equitable Credit for Unilateral Joint-Account Withdrawal ($6,400.00)
claims.statement: Certified joint checking statements (Ex. J) document Petitioner's unilateral $6,400.00 withdrawal on August 28, 2029, entitling Respondent to an equitable offset.

claims.title: Equal Statutory Access to School, Medical & Extracurricular Portals (§ 408)
claims.statement: Under Uniform Domestic Relations Act § 408, both parents hold equal statutory access to all academic, medical, dental, and extracurricular records regardless of residential schedule.
claims.summary: Uniform Act § 408 guarantees both parents equal access to all school and medical portals.

claims.title: Rebuttal of Proposed 90-Overnight Restriction as Unsupported by Statutory Factors
claims.statement: Petitioner's proposal to cut Respondent to 90 overnights/year (OP Ex. 1) is contradicted by the 2030 zero-tardy school record (Ex. K), 6-year caregiving history (Ex. B), and 512-yard transit verification (Ex. F).

traps.title: Dismissed Interim Administrative Petition (Oct 2029)

traps.openingAlignedPivot: That interim petition was dismissed by joint stipulation on November 18, 2029 with zero findings (Ex-J), and we have had nine incident-free months of structured co-parenting since.

traps.title: Alleged School Transit Corridor Proximity & Telemetry Log

traps.title: Speculative $14,000/mo Income Imputation on Retired Pensioner

traps.trapWarning: Do not debate hypothetical consulting rates from 2026.
traps.openingAlignedPivot: As the Court recognized at Temporary Orders (Ex-N ¶ 15), I have a certified full disability retirement determination (Ex-E), and the guidelines prohibit imputing speculative wages on top of verified disability benefits.

traps.title: Unpaid Civic Curriculum Research Mischaracterized as Commercial Consulting
traps.allegation: Opposing counsel points to public-interest educational repositories (OP-Ex-06) as proof of commercial consulting revenue.
traps.trapWarning: Do not get drawn into technical jargon; anchor in the IRS transcripts.
traps.openingAlignedPivot: Certified IRS transcripts from 2026 through 2029 (Ex-C, Ex-D) confirm $0.00 in consulting revenue, wages, or distributions; self-paced civic writing at home leaves me 100% available for all three minor children.

traps.title: Retroactive Nov 2029–May 2030 Expense Demand vs. $30,000.00 Escrow Omission
traps.allegation: Opposing counsel demands retroactive household reimbursement under the Nov 2029 interim stipulation (OP-Ex-12).
traps.trapWarning: Do not sound angry; let the Court's Temporary Orders ruling speak for itself.
traps.openingAlignedPivot: At Temporary Orders (Ex-N ¶¶ 24-26), the Court held that stipulation unconscionable because $30,000.00 in escrow accounts (Ex-H) had been omitted from the initial Sworn Financial Statement (Ex-G).

traps.title: Commercial $2,400/mo After-School Agency Demand vs. Free Parental Care

traps.trapWarning: Do not criticize Petitioner's regional travel schedule; frame your availability as a resource for both parents.

traps.title: Duplicate $320/mo Medical Insurance Add-On vs. Zero-Premium Statutory Plan

traps.openingAlignedPivot: Temporary Orders found zero basis to restrict my parenting time (Ex-N ¶ 8), and we successfully practiced equal 50/50 parenting time for 90 days in Summer 2030.

traps.title: Wednesday School Exchange Logistics & Calendar Notes

steps.action: Step 1 — Define My Matter & Relief Goals: Enter your case details, court, hearing date, and the specific outcomes you are asking the judge to order.
Step 2 — Build My Timeline & Documents: Add the key dates and events in your case and organize the documents or photos that support each fact.
Step 3 — Prepare for Tough Questions: Write down criticisms or allegations the other side might raise and rehearse calm, fact-based answers with flashcards.
Step 4 — Practice My Direct Testimony: Organize the questions you will answer in court, link each answer to your documents, and rehearse step-by-step.
Step 5 — Collaborate with Counsel & Export Packet: List questions for your attorney, check your hearing readiness, and download your .prismlegal.json file or printable summary.

steps.action: Step 1 — Matter Intake & Case Theory: Open a client's matter file or create a new docket, select the governing legal framework, and align on relief targets.

Step 3 — Witness Examinations & Evidentiary Objections: Script direct examinations and cross-examination impeachment, prepare objections, and budget hearing minutes.

pedagogyGuides.heading: Why Courts Ask for Specific Relief Orders First
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: A judge or hearing officer can only grant orders that are clearly stated and authorized by statute. Vague requests like 'be fair' are hard for a court to enforce, whereas concrete requests (such as a specific parenting schedule, a specific repair deadline, or a specific benefit effective date) give the court a clear roadmap.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: State each goal in one calm, forward-looking sentence describing the exact order you want the judge to sign, followed by the practical reason it helps your household or resolves the dispute.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Uniform Marriage & Divorce Act § 402 · URLTA § 4.104 · 38 C.F.R. § 3.102 · Scoped Unbundled Representation (ABA Model Rule 1.2(c))

pedagogyGuides.heading: How a Chronological Timeline & Linked Exhibits Build Credibility
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Hearings move quickly. When your facts are arranged in chronological order and linked to a specific record—such as a school log, certified notice, bank statement, or medical report—the judge can verify your testimony immediately.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Focus on observable dates, actions, and records rather than emotional characterizations. Whenever a document or photo proves an event, enter its Exhibit Label (e.g., Ex. A) so it links automatically.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Federal Rules of Evidence 401 (Relevance), 803(6) (Business Records), 803(8) (Public Records) & 901 (Authentication)

pedagogyGuides.heading: How to Handle Hostile Questions & Out-of-Context Quotes Calmly
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Cross-examination is often designed to provoke frustration or pull a single sentence from an email, text, or journal out of context. A calm, measured witness who answers directly and points to the complete written record wins the court's trust.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Pause for two seconds before answering. Never argue with opposing counsel. Acknowledge any undisputed baseline fact, then calmly direct the court to the full context and supporting exhibit.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Federal Rule of Evidence 106 (Rule of Completeness — Requiring Full Context for Partial Quotes) & Rule 611 (Mode and Order of Examining Witnesses)

pedagogyGuides.heading: How Direct Examination Establishes Your Case-in-Chief
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Direct examination is your opportunity to tell your story through open-ended questions ('Who, What, When, Where, How'). Unlike cross-examination, your attorney cannot ask leading questions on direct, so your answers must supply the concrete facts and introduce your exhibits.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Practice speaking in clear 2-to-3 sentence answers. When a question references an exhibit, identify the document, confirm how you recognize it, and state the key fact it shows.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Federal Rule of Evidence 602 (Personal Knowledge), Rule 611(c) (Non-Leading Direct Questions) & Rule 901(b)(1) (Testimony of Witness with Knowledge)

pedagogyGuides.heading: How to Review Case Consistency & Share with Counsel
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Before stepping into court or meeting with a legal-aid clinic or consulting attorney, checking that every goal is backed by timeline events, exhibits, and rehearsed testimony saves hours of preparation time.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Use the Automated Case Consistency Check below to spot any unlinked documents or unrehearsed questions, log your specific questions for counsel, and save your portable .prismlegal.json file.

pedagogyGuides.heading: Scoping the Engagement, Forum & Theory of the Case
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Whether appearing as full-scope trial counsel or providing unbundled limited-scope representation under Rule 1.2(c), defining the governing statutory framework, forum rules, and relief posture upfront anchors every downstream proof requirement.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Select the governing Area of Law and Representation Scope below. Use the one-click Domain Scaffolding tool to populate standard statutory elements if starting a fresh docket.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: ABA Model Rule 1.2(c) (Unbundled Legal Services), Rule 1.1 (Competence) & Pretrial Management Under Civil Rule 16

pedagogyGuides.heading: Mapping Statutory Elements, Proposed Findings & Rule Exceptions
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Trial courts must enter findings of fact and conclusions of law on each statutory element. An explicit proof matrix prevents evidentiary gaps, compiles each backed proposition into a proposed court finding, and pairs general rules with controlling statutory exceptions.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Ensure every claim is linked to at least one exhibit so the Refusal Guard clears it for your proposed findings. Record any statutory exceptions or immunities (such as protected disability income or mandatory-disclosure bars) in the Rule Exceptions drawer.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Civil Rule 52(a) (Findings and Conclusions by the Court), Rule 26(e) / 16.2 (Disclosure Duty) & Controlling Statutory Exceptions

pedagogyGuides.heading: Homeostatic Hearing Clock Budgeting & Examination Scripting
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Trial judges strictly enforce time limits. Overrunning direct or cross-examination can forfeit time needed for closing argument and final-order requests. Stage-by-stage budgeting protects your closing gate reserve.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Allocate realistic minutes to each witness and check the 4-Stage Hearing Clock breakdown below to verify that your Closing & Final Orders Gate reserve remains protected.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Federal Rule of Evidence 611(a) (Control by the Court Over Time and Mode of Examination) & Rule 103 (Preserving Evidentiary Rulings)

pedagogyGuides.heading: Auditing Admissibility Foundations, Chain of Custody & Guideline Math
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Even persuasive documents can be excluded if their authentication or hearsay exception foundation is not ready at counsel table. Likewise, support, rating, and damages requests must be backed by transparent statutory worksheet calculations.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Assign an explicit rule foundation (e.g., FRE 803(6), 803(8), 901) to every exhibit, optionally compute a local SHA-256 verification digest for digital files, and verify the statutory calculator outputs for your jurisdiction.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Federal Rules of Evidence 901–902 (Authentication), 803 (Hearsay Exceptions), Uniform Support Guidelines § 305, 38 C.F.R. § 4.25 & URLTA § 4.104

pedagogyGuides.heading: Consistency Audit, Priority Ranking & Trial Brief Handoff
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Before hearing day, counsel needs an automated check across all claims, exhibits, and witness scripts, a ranked priority order for examination themes if time is cut short, and written answers to client strategy questions.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Review the Automated Consistency Audit and Priority Strategy Schedule below, answer any open client questions, and export either the updated .prismlegal.json file or the compiled Markdown Trial Brief.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Civil Rule 16 (Pretrial Conferences and Trial Briefs), Rule 52(a) (Proposed Findings) & ABA Model Rule 1.4 (Client Alignment)

pedagogyGuides.heading: Live Witness Stand & Counsel Table Cross-Exam Responder
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: During live cross-examination, quick access to the exact rebuttal exhibit, the trap to avoid, the Rule 106 full-context citation, and the calm one-sentence answer keeps testimony focused on the court's statutory factors.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Click any topic pill below as soon as opposing counsel raises that subject to display the calm response and supporting exhibit in high-contrast large type.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Federal Rule of Evidence 106 (Remainder of Related Writings) & Rule 611(b) (Scope of Cross-Examination)

pedagogyGuides.heading: Live Direct Examination Checklist & Foundation Pacing
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Checking off each direct examination question as it is asked ensures that no required statutory element or exhibit admission offer is inadvertently skipped under courtroom time pressure.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Use the search filter or priority badges to track essential testimony points and offer each linked exhibit into evidence as soon as its foundation is laid.
pedagogyGuides.ruleContext: Federal Rules of Evidence 611(a), 602 & 901 (Offering Exhibits During Case-in-Chief)

pedagogyGuides.heading: Live Exhibit Offer & Admission Status Tracker
pedagogyGuides.whyItMatters: Before resting your case-in-chief, counsel must confirm that every exhibit relied upon for proposed findings or closing argument has been formally offered and admitted into the record.
pedagogyGuides.coachingTip: Update each exhibit's status to 'Offered at Hearing' or 'Admitted' in real time so you can verify your complete evidentiary record before resting.
